correctness.rationale: Rule 30 backward pair propagation has exact four-state truth tables T0=(0,2,3,3), T1=(2,0,1,1). An output ring has a same-length predecessor iff its composition has a pair-state fixed point, including n=1,2. The exact complete 41-element transformation closure yields a 41-state deterministic acceptor (30 accepting). The adjugate gives numerator degree at most 40 and denominator degree at most 41. The candidate rational expression has numerator/denominator degree seven; its cross-multiplied discrepancy has degree at most 48. All 49 exact coefficients n=0..48 match from a replayed certificate, proving equality for all lengths, not merely by finite extrapolation. An independently written direct Rule30 evaluator exhausts input rings through n=17; all 27 finite counts in Faulkenberry 2016 agree. Newton root-sum identities give recurrence and asymptotic.

originality.rationale: The contribution is an explicit proved all-n count and sharp asymptotic for the image of one-step Rule 30 on indexed n-cycles. Jen 1989 covers arbitrary finite-window preimages with free boundary, not same-period cyclic images. Faulkenberry 2016 already tabulates exactly this invariant at n=1..27 and Wolfram 2019 inspects selected small rings; neither inspected study establishes the all-length rational identity, closed cubic-root recurrence or exponential missing-output proportion. The published records searched did not produce a stronger all-n result. Priority is provisional because an unindexed equivalent or undownloaded historic full text could exist.
residual_risks: Unindexed or uncatalogued earlier results could supply the same all-period recurrence or rational image enumerator.

value.rationale: For a classical, left-permutive binary cellular automaton, finite-period image deficiency is a natural, exact measure of the tension between infinite-lattice surjectivity and lack of same-period predecessors. An all-period exact rational generating function and cubic-root decay rate give a structural answer beyond finite ring tables and reveal a sharp exponential proportion. It does not rely on generic numerical novelty or claim implications for unrelated dynamics.
